An Enquiry into the Causes of the Frequent Executions at Tyburn is a pamphlet by Bernard Mandeville, first printed in 1725. This edition is number 105 of the Augustan Reprint Society, issued by the William Andrews Clark Memorial Library at Los Angeles in 1964. Malvin Zirker supplied the introduction. Mandeville, the author of The Fable of the Bees, turned his sharp eye on London's hanging days.

The footnotes preserved in the copy show the introduction's range. One note discusses William Irwin's account of the career and fame of Jonathan Wild, the thief-taker general. Another points to Henry Fielding's later Enquiry into the Causes of the Late Increase of Robbers. A further note adds that the criminal-hero enjoyed the amorous admiration of the fair. When clever Tom Clinch rode by to execution, the maids ran to the doors and balconies.
38425-geographic-variation-in-the-north-:
Geographic Variation in the North American Cyprinid Fish Hybopsis Gracilis is a scientific paper by Leonard J Olund and Frank B Cross. It appeared in the publications of the University of Kansas museum of natural history. The issue is dated February ten, nineteen sixty one. It runs to some twenty six pages with plates and figures. Contents split the study into set parts.

An introduction and a section on methods and materials open the paper. A description of the species follows, with two subspecies treated in turn. Variation within the species takes its own section. Natural history comes next, with habitat, associated species, food, and spawning season. A discussion and a list of literature cited close the work. Ten counts of body characters and seventeen measurements form the basis of study, the text says.

Albrecht von Eyb was one of the earliest German humanists, born near Ansbach in Franconia in 1420 and dead in 1475. After early studies at Erfurt, he pursued humanistic learning at Pavia and Bologna in Italy. He returned to Germany in 1451 as canon of Eichstätt and Bamberg. He studied again at Bologna from 1452 to 1459, took his doctorate in canon and civil law, and served as chamberlain to Pope Pius II.

Eyb's best-known work is his Little Book on Marriage of 1472. It asks whether a wise man should take a lawful wife and finally decides in favour of married life. Its popularity shows in twelve reprints between 1472 and 1540. He also wrote the Margarita Poetica, a textbook of humanistic rhetoric gathering passages from Latin authors, and finished his Mirror of Morals in 1474.
doe-osti-2587043-intelligently-partition:
Min Xiong of the National Renewable Energy Laboratory leads a seventeen-author, six-institution team in this August 2025 report, NREL/TP-5D00-89823. Bin Wang, Deepthi Vaidhynathan, and colleagues from five other organizations share the work. The problem is simulating grids crowded with inverter-based resources such as solar and wind plants, whose fast controls can shake grid stability.

Standard phasor tools miss those fast dynamics, while full electromagnetic transient tools are too slow for very large systems. The team built an integrated platform, I-PEP, that partitions a grid between the two methods and runs each region with the tool that fits it. It also published ParaEMT, an open-source electromagnetic transient simulator built for parallel and cloud computing. A novel partitioning method was developed and validated along the way. The result is a path to studying dynamic events on grids with many buses and many inverters.
doe-osti-3402331-enhanced-preparation-fo:
Georgia Tech Research Corporation reports on EPICS, a project on smart cybermanufacturing, under award DE-EE0008303. Kyle Saleeby and Kate Fu led the work. The project ran from August 15, 2018 to October 31, 2024.

One strand built better sensors for factory machines. A device called WASP tracks machine vibration live and sends data to a phone app by Bluetooth. Its magnetic mount lets workers place and move sensors with care. Good placement matters, since a loose sensor gives bad data. The work aims to help shops catch faults early and plan upkeep with real signals.
